standard_prerequisites: The rig-smooth homomorphism definition via annihilation of Ext^1 of the completed naive cotangent complex
The approximation lemmas for complexes over adic rings from More on Algebra, giving exactness of the perturbed presentation and an isomorphism of associated graded rings for n large
The uniformity integers d and q of the associated graded, and the lifting lemma producing a homomorphism congruent to a prescribed one modulo a prescribed power
core_obligations: Choose the annihilation exponent c from rig-smoothness and the exactness constant c_1 from the approximation lemmas
Declare n = max(c_1 + 1, q_0 + (d_0 + 1)c, 2(d_0 + 1)c + 1) and build the canonical isomorphism B/I^n B to B'/I^n B' induced by the close presentation
Lift psi_n to an A-algebra homomorphism phi : B to B' congruent modulo I^{n - (d_0+1)c} using the lifting lemma
Prove phi is an isomorphism: surjectivity from completeness, injectivity from the induced surjective endomorphism of the associated graded being an isomorphism and Krull's intersection theorem
proof_roadmap: Set up the two constants c and c_1 and the uniformity data
Form the mod-I^n comparison isomorphism and apply the lifting lemma at the chosen n
Prove surjectivity of phi via the completion generalities lemma
Prove injectivity via the associated graded surjection being an isomorphism and Krull intersection
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is a deformation stability statement: a rig-smooth quotient of an I-adic polynomial algebra is isomorphic to any quotient by a presentation perturbed inside I^n for a suitable n (source lines 1362-1449, label lemma-close-enough). The solver must combine three independently produced constants (annihilation exponent, approximation constant, uniformity data) into one bound, lift the mod-I^n isomorphism to an actual homomorphism, and then prove it is an isomorphism through a surjective-endomorphism-of-Noetherian-ring argument plus Krull intersection; the constant assembly and the injectivity route are substantive. Allowed background: the cited More on Algebra approximation lemmas and the uniformity section, delivered as navigation pointers.
